content.text:
## What works

- `src/automation/server.py:46` acquires `self.dataset_lease=Lease(self.config)` before constructing NativeBackend. Contention is therefore rejected before native startup writes.
- `scripts/engine_reload_patch.py:26` sets `loaded.test = true; loaded.signal;`, and line 28 waits before releasing the engine lock. This respects SuperCollider’s [Condition semantics](https://docs.supercollider.online/Classes/Condition.html) and covers asynchronous allocation completion.
- `tests/maiden_browser.cjs:48` requires `fs.readFileSync(local(info.script),'utf8')===changed`, then checks changed native MIDI. This verifies an actual save/run outcome. All four recorded evidence hashes match their manifest; I inspected those records without rerunning tests.

## What doesn't work

- **[MAJOR] Dataset validation breaks existing symlinked application launches.** `src/automation/datasets.py:12–15` uses `entry=Path(config['script']).resolve()` followed by `entry.relative_to(root)`. However, `src/app_fixtures.py:26` deliberately creates profile directories using `link.symlink_to(code/app,target_is_directory=True)`: resolving the script moves it outside the selected profile root. Existing `--fixture mosaic` launches—and generic applications assembled through equivalent directory links—now fail with `dataset_mapping`, even without Maiden or reopening. Preserve the runtime’s declared relative mapping rather than checking containment after dereferencing the application link.

- **[MAJOR] Failed saves are reported as successful, and Run executes the old file.** The integrated pinned frontend, `.runtime/maiden-02/source/web/src/model/edit-actions.js:278`, unconditionally calls `dispatch(bufferSaveSuccess(resource, response.entity))`; line 279 also invokes the completion callback. A read-only file produces HTTP 500 from Maiden, but its reducer still executes `.set('modified', false)` at `web/src/model/edit-reducers.js:295`, and Save-and-Run proceeds. This contradicts the claimed exact-save workflow: the editor appears saved while disk contents remain unchanged. Check HTTP success, retain dirty text on failure, show the error, and suppress Run.

- **[MAJOR] Cleanup failure becomes a permanent no-op on retry, while dataset ownership is released.** `src/automation/server.py:63–64` executes `if self.closed:return` and sets `self.closed=True` before cleanup; line 76 releases the lease even when a closer fails. Native cleanup can exit before finishing its process loop—for example, the final `process.wait(timeout=3)` at `src/runtime/native.py:564` can raise. A subsequent restart skips cleanup and starts another session against the released dataset, leaving unfinished native processes behind. Separate “reject new work” from “cleanup completed”; retry unfinished cleanup and retain writer ownership until native writers have stopped.

- **[MINOR] Reopened data disappears as a navigable Maiden directory.** `patches/maiden/0001-follow-directory-links.patch:12` resolves links only inside `listingHandler`. The untouched root handler at `.runtime/maiden-02/source/cmd/server.go:238` still uses `ioutil.ReadDir(s.dustRoot())`, and line 930 determines children using `entry.IsDir()`. Restart/reopen makes `dust/data` a symlink (`src/runtime/native.py:115`), so the root response presents it as a file. Apply the same link handling to root listings and verify data navigation after restart.

- **[MINOR] Failed re-verification leaves a successful report flag.** `tests/maiden_cleanup.py:29` records `r['verification_error']=repr(error)` but never resets an existing `r['passed']=True`; line 30 writes that contradictory report back. Rechecking previously successful evidence after a WAV disappears therefore exits unsuccessfully while retaining machine-readable success. Reset `passed` before verification and remove stale verification errors after success.

## Risks

- **[MINOR] Recovery can certify stale build outputs as carrying current patches.** `scripts/build_maiden.py:29` checks only that patches reverse-apply to source, while line 30 checks merely ELF magic and the existence of `web/build/index.html`. Applying a frontend patch after an interrupted build, then finalizing without rebuilding, records the new patch set against old assets. Verify the recovered source against the archive plus declared patches and rebuild affected outputs before recording their identity.

## Gaps

- **[MAJOR] Restart failure/retry and held-input isolation lack acceptance coverage.** `tests/maiden_lifecycle.cjs:51` requires the first restart response to be `200`; session switching at lines 35–38 uses completed encoder clicks. Neither path exercises replacement startup failure, cleanup failure, retry, or an input held across switching/restart. Add bounded cases that verify explicit failure, subsequent recovery, writer-lock ownership, absent old processes, and unaffected peer input state. The existing SC-error test proves successful recovery from an interpreter error, not these lifecycle failure paths.

## Improvements

Nothing notable.
